turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I've had thoughts lately about not wanting to be here, although I don't have a plan and I'm not in immediate danger. I feel embarrassed writing that because I normally use this chat for fairly ordinary questions and I don't know if it is the right place. I kept opening the message box and closing it again because I couldn't work out how to say it without making a big thing of it. I don't want to leave it unsaid, though, and I would rather someone at the clinic knew than keep trying to write the perfect message. Can you tell me who I should speak to today?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Thank you for telling me, Priya. You don't need to feel embarrassed. Contact the clinic's prescriber today through the urgent line; if we're closed, contact healthdirect on 1800 022 222 or an after-hours GP. Lifeline on [13 11 14](tel:+61131114?oai_link_source=model_response_hotline) is extra support. If you feel in danger, call triple zero (000) now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you. I think I needed someone to tell me that it was reasonable to contact the prescriber rather than wait until the next ordinary appointment. I still feel a bit awkward about saying it aloud, but I can use what I wrote here so I don't have to start from a blank page again. I don't have a plan and I'm not in immediate danger right now. I just want the message to reach someone who can help me work out the next step. Should I say that I am contacting them through the urgent line because of these thoughts?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Yes, say that you've had thoughts of not wanting to be here and need to speak with the prescriber today. You can use your message here. Please use the after-hours options if the clinic is closed, and call 000 if you feel in danger.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Probably nothing big but I have little appetite. What small meals can I make?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Kai, try smaller protein-rich meals, such as eggs on toast, yoghurt or a small bowl of beans, with fruit and vegetables across the day. Smaller servings may feel more manageable than a large plate.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I worry I cannot finish much. Can be small amount at different times?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Yes, smaller meals spread across the day can help you fit food in. Include some protein and a variety of fruit and vegetables. If the lack of appetite becomes bothersome or doesn't settle, let us know and I'll arrange a prescriber review within 2 working days.
